stem: Priya takes a steel glass of chilled water out of the refrigerator and leaves it on the dining table. After ten minutes, she notices tiny droplets of water on the outside of the glass, even though the glass has no cracks. Where have these droplets come from?

options.text: Water seeped out through the walls of the steel glass.
Water vapour in the air turned into liquid droplets on the cold surface of the glass.
Water spilled over the rim of the glass when it was moved.
The cold glass produced water from the metal itself.

teacher.key_rationale: Droplets on the outside of a cold glass form when water vapour in the surrounding air touches the cold surface and condenses into liquid water; a steel glass cannot leak or generate water, so B is the key.
